Thanks — putting proposed guardrails in writing so everyone has the same expectation. High level: we can accommodate a retroactive credit for prior-period SKU misallocations, but we need a narrowly tailored amendment that:

1) Limits lookback to a single fiscal quarter prior to the amendment effective date (90 days).
2) Specifies that credits are issued as a contra-invoice (negative invoice) applied to the next invoice cycle rather than reissuing historical invoices. We will not issue refunds to a bank account unless agreed in advance for exceptional cases.
3) Handles caps/floors: when a pack-swap changes the unit mix, the amendment will instruct that the pricing exhibit be interpreted using the per-SKU unit prices from the applicable exhibit; caps/floors remain effective and the credit calculation uses the existing per-unit exhibit prices (i.e., we do not re-run the annualized banding or change the floor for the prior period retroactively).
4) Includes a maximum cumulative credit exposure of USD 100,000 or 20% of the quarter's billable value (whichever is lower) to cap risk.
5) Requires a signed Amendment and a Customer-issued PO referencing DEAL-3197 before any credit is processed.

Draft amendment language (suggested insertion to Pricing Exhibit):
"In the event of an inadvertent SKU misallocation identified by Customer within ninety (90) days following the end of the applicable invoicing quarter, Customer may request a retroactive credit. Redwood Inference will calculate any credit using the per-SKU unit prices set forth in Exhibit A as applied to the quantities originally billed. Credits will be issued as contra-invoices applied to Customer's next invoice cycle, subject to a maximum aggregate credit of the lesser of USD 100,000 or twenty percent (20%) of the total billed amount for the affected quarter. Any credit is conditional upon execution of a mutually agreed Amendment and Customer's issuance of a purchase order referencing the Amendment and DEAL-3197."
Operational notes: Finance will require the signed amendment and a PO at time of processing. Please also include a one-line summary in the amendment that the pack-swap is permitted as an exhibit adjustment (so we don't change core order terms).

Laura / Sofia: if we agree to these guardrails, I can convert the snippet above into a redline for Pricing_Exhibit-markup.docx and send back to Jordan.
